items.title: Sudden Death, and Bodies Left Behind

items.zh: 除北拘盧洲，餘一切處悉有中夭。又人、鬼、傍生趣有餘滓身；天及那落迦與識俱沒，無餘滓身。
items.en: Except for Uttarakuru, every other place has premature death. Further, in the destinies of humans, ghosts, and animals, a remaining body is left behind; for gods and hell-beings, consciousness simply vanishes together with the body, leaving no remaining body at all.

items.title: Three Kinds of Enjoyment, and Each Realm's Characteristic Suffering

items.zh: 受用建立者，略有三種。謂受用苦樂、受用飲食、受用婬欲。
items.en: As for establishing enjoyment: briefly, there are three kinds — the enjoyment of pleasure and pain, the enjoyment of food and drink, and the enjoyment of sexual activity.

items.zh: 受用苦樂者，謂那落迦有情多分受用極治罰苦；傍生有情多分受用相食噉苦；餓鬼有情多分受用極飢渴苦；人趣有情多分受用匱乏追求種種之苦；天趣有情多分受用衰惱墜沒之苦。
items.en: As for the enjoyment of pleasure and pain: hell-beings, for the most part, undergo the pain of extreme punishment; animals, for the most part, undergo the pain of devouring one another; hungry ghosts, for the most part, undergo the pain of extreme hunger and thirst; those in the human destiny, for the most part, undergo the pain of scarcity and endless seeking; and those in the heavenly destiny, for the most part, undergo the pain of decline and falling.

items.zh: 又於等活大那落迦中，多受如是極治罰苦。謂彼有情，多共聚集，業增上生，種種苦具次第而起，更相殘害，悶絕躄地。次虛空中有大聲發，唱如是言：此諸有情可還等活！可還等活！次彼有情欻然復起，復由如前所說苦具更相殘害。由此因緣，長時受苦，乃至先世所造一切惡不善業未盡未出。故此那落迦名為等活。
items.en: Further, in the Reviving Hell, beings for the most part undergo just such extreme punishment as this: these beings, gathered together in great numbers through the compounding force of their own karma, find one instrument of suffering after another arising against them, and set upon one another until they collapse senseless to the ground. Then, in the open sky, a great voice cries out, saying: "Let these beings revive! Let them revive!" — and they suddenly rise up again, only to set upon one another once more with the same instruments of suffering as before. Through this cause, they undergo suffering for a long time, for as long as the unwholesome karma created in past lives remains unexhausted and unresolved. This is why this hell is called Reviving.

items.zh: 又於黑繩大那落迦中，多受如是治罰重苦。謂彼有情多分為彼所攝獄卒以黑繩拼之，或為四方、或為八方、或為種種圖畵文像。彼既拼已，隨其處所，若鑿、若斲、若斫、若剜。由如是等種種因緣，長時受苦，乃至先世所造一切惡不善業未盡未出。故此那落迦名為黑繩。
items.en: Further, in the Black-Rope Hell, beings for the most part undergo grave punishment such as this: guardians belonging to that hell bind them with black ropes, marking them into squares, or into octagons, or into various patterned designs, and then, following those very markings, drill, chisel, hack, and gouge them. This is why this hell is called Black-Rope.

items.zh: 又於眾合大那落迦中，多受如是治罰重苦。謂彼有情，或時展轉聚集和合，爾時便有彼攝獄卒驅逼令入兩鐵羺頭大山之間。彼既入已，兩山迫之；既被迫已，一切門中血便流注。如兩鐵羺頭，如是兩鐵羝頭、兩鐵馬頭、兩鐵象頭、兩鐵師子頭、兩鐵虎頭亦爾。
items.en: Further, in the Crushing Hell, beings for the most part undergo grave punishment such as this: gathered together at times, they are then driven by that hell's guardians in between two great mountains shaped like iron ram-heads. Once driven in, the two mountains close upon them, crushing them until blood streams from every opening of the body. As with the two iron ram-heads, so too with two iron goat-heads, two iron horse-heads, two iron elephant-heads, two iron lion-heads, and two iron tiger-heads.

items.zh: 復令和合，置大鐵槽中，便即壓之，如壓甘蔗。既被壓已，血便流注。復和合已，有大鐵山從上而墮，令彼有情躄在鐵地，若斫若刺，或擣或裂。既被斫刺及擣裂已，血便流注。由此因緣，長時受苦，乃至先世所作一切惡不善業未盡未出。故此那落迦名為眾合。又於號叫大那落迦中，多受如是治罰重苦。
items.en: They bring them together again, put them in a great iron trough, and press them like sugar cane. When they have been pressed, the blood flows out. When they have been brought together again, a great iron mountain falls from above, knocking those beings flat on the iron ground, where they are hacked or stabbed, pounded or torn apart. When they have been hacked, stabbed, pounded, and torn apart, the blood flows out. Because of this, they suffer for a long time, until all the evil, unwholesome karma they did in former lives is exhausted and spent. That is why this hell is called Crushing. Further, in the great Wailing hell, beings mostly undergo heavy punishments of the following kind.

blocks.text: Today the survey turns from measurements to experience. After a note on untimely death and on which beings leave a body behind, the treatise begins the fifth aspect of the realms, **enjoyment**, starting with pleasure and pain. It names the predominant pain of each of the five destinies and then describes the first of the eight hot hells. These descriptions are vivid. Our teachers read them neither as horror stories nor as mere symbols, but as the treatise intends: as the experienced result of particular karma, given so that we take karma seriously.

Two passages are missing from Ru-Yi's translation (now supplied in our own translation, marked as ours): 0296a04–a11 (in the Crushing Hell, beings are pressed in a great iron trough like sugar-cane until blood flows, then an iron mountain falls on them and they are hacked and torn on the iron ground) and 0296a18 ("in the great Burning Hell beings mostly undergo such heavy punishments").

subs.head: Untimely death, and the body left behind

blocks.text: Except in Uttarakuru, beings may die before their lifespan is complete (Day 4). When they die, humans, ghosts, and animals leave a body behind; gods and hell-beings vanish together with their consciousness, leaving nothing. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Pīxún jì*, explains why: egg-born, womb-born, and moisture-born beings leave corpses, while gods and hell-beings are entirely transformation-born (Day 13) and leave none.
"Enjoyment" (受用) covers three things: **pleasure and pain**, **food and drink**, and **sexual activity**. Fascicle 4 treats only the first; the others come later.

subs.head: The predominant pain of each destiny

blocks.text: Each destiny has its characteristic suffering, "for the most part":

items: animals: **devouring one another**. Master Cháng Bǎi: "the familiar food chain";
humans: **scarcity and seeking** (匱乏追求), never having enough and always pursuing;

blocks.text: The phrase "for the most part" matters. Each destiny's suffering is its dominant tone, not the only one. Notice also that the gods are not exempt; Day 28 will describe their suffering in detail.

The first hot hell is **Reviving** (等活). Beings there attack one another with whatever weapon appears in their hands, until they collapse; then "a great voice cries out in the sky: 'Let these beings revive!'" and they rise again to fight. Master Cháng Bǎi: dying and reviving over and over, with no end until the karma is spent. The image is hatred repeating itself without exhausting itself.
In the **Black-Rope Hell** (黑繩), guardians mark the body with black lines into squares or patterns and cut along them. The precision is part of the horror.

In the **Crushing Hell** (眾合), beings are driven between two great mountains shaped like the heads of rams, goats, horses, elephants, lions, and tigers, which close upon them "until blood streams from every opening". The passage missing from Ru-Yi adds being pressed in an iron trough like sugar-cane and crushed under falling iron mountains.

These passages are uncomfortable. Two things help. First, everything here follows the principle of Day 10: no outside judge sends anyone to hell. On Day 6 we saw that a being is drawn to its birthplace by its own mistaken perception and craving. Second, Day 24 reminded us how long these lives last. The point of describing them is the one Master Cháng Bǎi makes again and again: a moment of anger or cruelty now is not small, because of what it can grow into. Venerable Miào Jìng's practical conclusion throughout is the same: guard the mind while it is still possible to choose.

quiz.q: The text says humans, ghosts, and animals leave a remaining body, while gods and hell-beings vanish with consciousness, leaving none. According to Master Cháng Bǎi (citing the Pixunji), why?
options: because gods and hell-beings never die
because gods' bodies are too large
egg-, womb-, and moisture-born beings leave corpses; gods and hell-beings are entirely spontaneously born and leave none
because hell-guardians take the corpses away
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Egg-born, womb-born, and moisture-born beings all leave corpses when they die. Spontaneously born beings do not … gods and all hell-beings are spontaneously born and leave no corpse." Some humans, ghosts, and animals are also spontaneously born, so the remaining body is said only of the others. The same section adds that everywhere except Uttarakuru, premature death occurs.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the three kinds of enjoyment?
options: pleasure and pain, food and drink, and sexual activity
quiz.why: "As for establishing enjoyment: briefly, there are three kinds — the enjoyment of pleasure and pain, the enjoyment of food and drink, and the enjoyment of sexual activity." Fascicle 4 covers only the first; food and sex follow in fascicle 5. "Enjoyment" here is neutral — undergoing pain is also "enjoyed."

quiz.q: Which pairing of the five destinies with their predominant pain is entirely correct?
options: hells–extreme punishment; animals–devouring one another; ghosts–extreme hunger and thirst; humans–scarcity and seeking; gods–decline and falling
quiz.why: The text lists them destiny by destiny, and the translation matches each: 極治罰苦 "extreme punishment," 相食噉苦 "devouring one another," 極饑渴苦 "extreme hunger and thirst," 匱乏追求種種之苦 "scarcity and endless seeking," 衰惱墜沒之苦 "decline and falling." §26 onward unfolds each line.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, why is the Reviving Hell so named?
options: beings maul one another until they collapse; a great voice in the sky cries "Let them revive!" and they rise again to resume
quiz.why: "Then, in the open sky, a great voice cries out, saying: 'Let these beings revive! Let them revive!' — and they suddenly rise up again … This is why this hell is called Reviving." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Dying and then living again is called Reviving." It continues until the past unwholesome karma is exhausted.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the torment of the Black-Rope Hell?
options: being burned in an iron chamber
guardians mark the body with black ropes into squares, octagons, or patterns, then drill, chisel, hack, and gouge along the lines
quiz.why: "Guardians belonging to that hell bind them with black ropes, marking them into squares, or into octagons, or into various patterned designs, and then, following those very markings, drill, chisel, hack, and gouge them." A is the Crushing Hell, B the Wailing Hell, D the cold hells.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, where are the beings of the Crushing Hell driven?
options: between two great mountains shaped like iron ram-heads (and goat, horse, elephant, lion, and tiger heads), which close until blood streams from every opening
quiz.why: "They are then driven by that hell's guardians in between two great mountains shaped like iron ram-heads. Once driven in, the two mountains close upon them, crushing them until blood streams from every opening of the body." Master Cháng Bǎi likens them to iron ram-heads closing in. A is the Burning Hell; C and D are gardens of the neighbouring hells.
